findings.title: The merged-band split is wrong on rectangular merged PHASE bands: every split ties, the lowest grid line wins, and the landing line ends up outside its own slot
findings.detail: When the two adjacent PHASE slots have the same u-extent, the merged band is a plain rectangle. Every candidate boundary then gives the same symmetric difference, so `_best_split` takes the lowest one (lo + 0.5 mm). It never considers what each slot has to contain (the landing line, the die row), which the replaced rule did. The result is a twin whose copper is identical (symdiff 0, so no twin gate can catch it), but whose HS-landing PHASE slot is 0.5 mm tall and lies below its own landing line. Example: generator v = [(16.5, 19.5), (19.5, 30.5)], twin v = [(16.5, 17.0), (17.0, 30.5)], landing line at 17.5. This is a regression: the removed midpoint-of-needs rule recovered the generator's boundary in 47/179 cases and always placed it between the needs. It also corrupts move 1 of the degradation rule, which is to be frozen in E008. From the twin's slots, `narrow_landing` reports the PHASE landing band as 'before_mm 0.5 -> after_mm 1.0' and leaves the copper essentially unchanged, so the L1 ratio is 1.40 / 1.92 / 1.70 / 1.60 instead of 2.24 / 2.87 / 2.71 / 2.61 from the generator's own slots. A rectangular PHASE pad that carries the LS dies and receives the HS wires is the usual half-bridge DBC pattern, so judged references are likely to hit this case. The generator's sampler happens never to produce equal ends (0 of 974 sampled merged layouts), which is why the tests pass. The claim of an 'exact merged-band split ... so that the slots are those of the generator' is false for this class.
findings.evidence: I built DRC-clean generator-space Params by setting both merged PHASE slots to a common u-extent (`D.build` plus `check` clean; 179 cases, n=2..4, k=1..3, all in role order (land, die)). `W.twin` boundary equal to the generator's: 0/179. Boundary between the landing line and the die row: 22/179. The emulated old rule: 47/179 and 179/179. `W.degrade` from the true slots vs from the twin's slots (n=2, k=1, seeds 70210-70212): ratios 2.2392 vs 1.4018, 2.8719 vs 1.9202, 2.706 vs 1.6964, 2.6057 vs 1.6027; the twin's widths read HS_landing_PHASE before_mm 0.5, after_mm 1.0.
findings.suggested_check: Restrict `_best_split` candidates to [end of the lower slot's need, start of the upper slot's need], break flat ties at the old midpoint of needs, and add a unit test on a rectangular merged band built with `D.build`.

findings.title: The tie test does not test a tie, and no test covers a flat symmetric difference
findings.detail: `test_best_split_is_the_minimum_symmetric_difference_boundary_with_lower_tie` uses an L-shaped band with a unique minimum at v = 3. No tie occurs, so the tie rule (the source of the blocker) is never exercised. `test_equal_interval_merged_bands_recover_the_generators_slots` only samples generator layouts, which never have equal slot ends.
findings.evidence: Test body: poly = box(0,0,10,3) ∪ box(0,3,6,7), so the minimum is unique.
findings.suggested_check: Add a rectangular-band case to the unit tests.

findings.title: The comment in `_fit` still describes the removed rule
findings.detail: The comment at twin.py lines 311-313 still says equal or partly overlapping intervals are split at 'the grid line between what each slot needs, inside the overlap'. That was the old rule. The code now takes the minimum-symmetric-difference boundary over the whole union.

findings.title: The walk hill-climbs on the screen it is judged by and stops just above the target
findings.detail: The walk picks whichever single-parameter change raises L1 most, so it actively selects changes where L1 may be biased. The 0.11 margin was derived from the bias band of generator layouts, not from walk outputs. The reached ratios sit just above the target (1.3875; confirmed median 1.3943), so the L2 ratio of a walk-produced D has almost no slack beyond the margin. In my single walk case the ratio was stable under L1 mesh refinement (1.3940 / 1.3903 / 1.3919 at hmax 4 / 2 / 1 mm). The docstring already defers verification to E008's L2 ratio.
findings.evidence: n=2, k=1, 2 mm rule, seed 2017 idx 7: 2 walk steps, ratio 1.3940 at hmax 4 mm, 1.3903 at hmax 2 mm, 1.3919 at hmax 1 mm.
findings.suggested_check: E008 should gate on the L2 ratio of every walk-produced D, not only record it.

findings.title: Small issues in the stress test
findings.detail: The first alternative of the terminal-state assertion, 'no single-parameter change raises', can never match: the message reads 'no single-parameter change of N DRC-valid raises'. A failure with no walk steps is recorded as ratio 1.0, not the ratio after moves 1-3. The test is marked slow and is not part of the definition-of-done commands, so the gate does not check the locked 63/72 figure. I ran it separately and it passes.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition-of-done commands: `pytest tests/unit/generate` 66 passed; `pytest -m 'not slow' tests/unit` 807 passed; `ruff check .` clean; thermal_fem.py hash a216d5fe3209bcee matches; `mfos gate --fast` 'all gates passed'.
Ran the slow stress regression tests/regression/test_degrade_walk_stress.py: passed in 533 s; '63 reached, 9 stuck; ratios min 1.3875 median 1.3943 max 2.0866', matching the locked values.

Twin-split sweep on 974 merged generator layouts (default and 2 mm rules, n=2..4, k=1..3, 40 seeds each): 0 slot mismatches, 134 `_best_split` calls, 0 twin errors. The fix works on the sampled population.

Adversarial case: 179 rectangular merged PHASE bands built with `D.build` and DRC-clean. The new rule recovers the generator's boundary 0/179 times and lies between the needs in 22/179; the emulated old rule gives 47/179 and 179/179.
Compared `degrade` from the generator's slots vs from the twin's slots on 4 rectangular-band cases: the twin-based L1 ratio is 35-40% lower, and the PHASE landing width is recorded as 0.5 -> 1.0 mm.
Checked mesh sensitivity of the walk with L1 at hmax 4 / 2 / 1 mm on 3 degraded layouts (seed 2017; idx 7 used the walk): ratios stable within about 0.01.
Read the DRC code: terminals off copper and wire landing margins are checked, so the walk cannot detach terminals or landings without `_try` rejecting the change.
Checked that the walk covers parameter indices 4..39 (`N_COPPER_PARAMS` = 40), i.e. 72 candidates per step, consistent with the docstring.
caveats: The rectangular-band case comes from Params I constructed by hand, not from the generator's sampler, which never produced equal slot ends in 974 merged samples. On the sampled generator population the new split is exact. The defect bites on references whose merged PHASE band is a rectangle.
I checked the walk's L1 robustness on only one walk-produced layout and did not run an L2 check.
